Yes. While rewriting quantize_bvh for the child-pair layout I wrote the new function using kInvalidNode, then ran `grep -rn 'kInvalidNode' src/pt_bvh.cpp include/*.hpp | head; grep -n 'constexpr\|static const' src/pt_bvh.cpp | head` (history message #140). It showed exactly one match for kInvalidNode — src/pt_bvh.cpp:399, `std::vector<unsigned int> block(bvh.nodes.size(), kInvalidNode);`, i.e. only the line I had just added — and the constants listing showed the file's only such definition was `constexpr float kInfinity = 1e30f;` at line 21. So kInvalidNode was referenced but never defined anywhere in src/ or include/, which is why I then added `constexpr unsigned int kInvalidNode = 0xFFFFFFFFu;` next to kInfinity (messages #141-#143) before switching the API to PtBvhChild. I know this from the archived tool result #140, which I just re-read in full rather than recalling.

Yes. After I rewrote quantize_bvh to emit the 32-byte child-pair blocks, I suspected the new code referenced kInvalidNode without it being defined, so I ran `grep -rn 'kInvalidNode' src/pt_bvh.cpp include/*.hpp | head` together with `grep -n 'constexpr\|static const' src/pt_bvh.cpp | head` (tool result in my history as message #140).

It showed exactly two things:
1. One single hit for kInvalidNode — `src/pt_bvh.cpp:399: std::vector<unsigned int> block(bvh.nodes.size(), kInvalidNode);` — which was my own brand-new line inside quantize_bvh. There was no declaration of it anywhere in pt_bvh.cpp or in any header under include/, so the name was undefined and the build would have failed.
2. The constexpr grep listed only `21:constexpr float kInfinity = 1e30f;`, which told me the file's convention for file-local constants and gave me the place to add it. I then defined kInvalidNode next to kInfinity at the top of src/pt_bvh.cpp (my notes in #141/#143 record that step) before switching the API (pt_bvh.hpp signature, pt_main.cpp vector type, pt_metal_host.mm sizeof) to PtBvhChild.

I know this because #140 is the verbatim tool result of that grep in my own session history, and #139/#141 are my notes immediately before and after it ("quantize_bvh rewritten but uses undefined kInvalidNode. Add it next to kInfinity"). For context, that child-pair experiment was ultimately rejected: bit-identical on all three scenes but a statistical wash against the _b baseline over 41 paired A/B rounds (mean +0.104 ± 0.218 ms), and the tree was reverted.
